P01.rationale: The speaker on stage serves as a large, prominent human anchor that dominates the left side of the page.

P05.rationale: While there are portraits in the background banner and foreground audience members, they lack clear framing or naming as distinct case study anchors compared to the references.

P07.rationale: There is no dedicated social-proof apparatus like a press wall or review grid; the only text resembling proof is small and buried in the background banner.

P10.rationale: The large typographic elements on the projection screen function as oversized decorative ghost numerals/glyphs that frame the composition.

P11.rationale: There are no real data-visualisations bound to numbers; the charts and graphs in the background banner appear empty or generic without specific metrics.

P12.rationale: The page reads as a dense, magazine-quality editorial layout that fills the sheet with overlapping layers of text and imagery.

P13.rationale: An intentional background atmosphere is created through the blurred audience heads and ambient lighting, adding depth rather than flat blankness.

P14.rationale: The foreground audience members act as a natural scrim for the overlaid text, though the projection screen itself remains bright white without darkening treatment.

P16.rationale: No device or product mockup is shown; the imagery focuses on people and presentation equipment rather than specific products.

N07.rationale: The imagery looks somewhat generic/stock-like due to the posed nature of the speaker and the blurred audience, lacking specific business context.

N08.rationale: There is minimal dead whitespace; the composition is tightly packed with text blocks and visual elements throughout the frame.

N10.rationale: Text sits directly on busy photo areas (the projection screen) without sufficient scrim or darkening to ensure readability.
